summary: Generate, dedupe and adversarially vet 25+ non-mainstream alt-data signals for earnings-event trading (Phase 1)

seeds.name: Satellite parking-lot car counts (benchmark only)
seeds.sector_focus: Consumer discretionary: big-box and specialty retail, restaurants, auto dealers with surface parking
seeds.mechanism: Cars parked at a chain's stores during the quarter proxy visit counts; visits times ticket size approximate same-store sales, the main driver of the quarter's revenue and operating leverage for box retailers, casual-dining chains and dealer groups. The chain is direct only where the lot is dedicated, visible from orbit and the format is car-dependent (suburban big-box, dealers), and it breaks for mall, urban and e-commerce-heavy names.
seeds.measurement_window: Vendor products deliver near-daily counts with 1-3 day latency, so the full fiscal-quarter count is final 2-5 days after quarter end, roughly 20-40 days before the release. With free imagery there is no usable reading: Sentinel-2 (10 m) and Landsat (30 m) pixels are larger than a car (REASONED), so counting needs 30-50 cm commercial imagery.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~6%: about 80 names in big-box/specialty retail, casual dining and dealer groups, e.g. Academy Sports (ASO), Floor & Decor (FND), Ollie's (OLLI), Dillard's (DDS), Texas Roadhouse (TXRH), Lithia (LAD), CarMax (KMX)

seeds.cost: $0 version does not exist; counts require sub-meter imagery or a vendor feed priced far above $100/month (REASONED; typical hedge-fund data contracts are five to six figures per year). Treat as a benchmark, not a buildable signal.
seeds.who_already_knows: Sell-side retail analysts and most quant funds buy the vendor counts. LITERATURE: Katona, Painter, Patatoukas and Zeng, 'On the Capital Market Consequences of Big Data: Evidence from Outer Space' (JFQA 2025, SSRN 2018) show satellite parking signals predict earnings surprises and that sophisticated traders capture the gap before the release; Zhu, 'Big Data as a Governance Mechanism' (RFS 2019) uses the same data. Assume mostly priced in by T-1.
seeds.vendors_selling_similar: Orbital Insight, RS Metrics (satellite counts); Placer.ai, Advan, SafeGraph (mobile foot traffic as a substitute)
seeds.why_ours_differs: It does not: there is no cheaper, faster or more granular free version. Keep as the crowdedness-1 reference point against which the other physical ideas are judged, and drop as a trade.
seeds.falsifiable_hypothesis: A positive change of 1 standard deviation in year-over-year quarterly parking-lot car counts (vendor feed) over the fiscal quarter, measured 5 days before the earnings release, predicts a positive T-1 to T+2 abnormal return versus the sector ETF and a positive revenue surprise, controlling for consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum. Expectation: coefficient positive but insignificant after 2018 because the signal is already traded.
seeds.industry_context: Store-based retailers and restaurants live or die on traffic, and same-store sales is the number the stock moves on at earnings. Parking lots are the only part of that traffic visible from orbit, which is why satellite vendors built the first commercial alternative-data products on them.
seeds.strongest_reason_wrong: The literature shows the gap closes before the release as institutional buyers of the feed trade it; counts miss basket size, online mix and price, and weather and holidays shift lots without shifting sales.
seeds.seed_item_extended: [physical] Satellite parking-lot car counts (use only as a crowded benchmark; assume mostly priced in)

vet.reject_reason: No $0 or $100/month version exists: free Sentinel-2 (10 m) and Landsat (30 m) pixels are larger than a car, and the only usable inputs are paid sub-metre imagery or vendor counts priced far above budget. The signal is crowdedness-1 by the candidate's own admission and the JFQA paper shows the gap is captured by sophisticated traders before the release. Retain the citation as the reference point for crowding in the write-up, but it is not a buildable or tradeable signal for this program.

seeds.name: VIIRS night-light and thermal activity at single large plants
seeds.sector_focus: Materials and energy: aluminum and steel mills, refineries, chemical complexes, cement kilns, coke plants
seeds.mechanism: Continuous-process plants (smelters, blast furnaces and EAFs, refineries, crackers, kilns) emit light and heat roughly in proportion to whether and how hard they run; a line idling or an unplanned outage darkens and cools the site within a day. For companies whose quarter depends on one to three such sites, days of darkness during the quarter map directly to lost volumes, under-absorbed fixed costs and a revenue/margin miss, and resumption dates feed next-quarter guidance.
seeds.measurement_window: Daily VIIRS radiance (Black Marble VNP46A2, 500 m) and 375 m thermal anomalies (FIRMS) with 1-3 day latency; the full-quarter site-days-active reading is final about 3 days after quarter end, roughly 20-40 days before the release. Landsat 8/9 thermal (100 m) adds detail every 8 days but with cloud gaps.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~5%: about 60 names with a few dominant continuous-process sites, e.g. Century Aluminum (CENX), Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF), SunCoke (SXC), PBF Energy (PBF), Delek (DK), Olin (OLN), Tronox (TROX), LSB Industries (LXU), Eagle Materials (EXP)

seeds.cost: $0: free Earthdata Login for Black Marble and a free FIRMS MAP_KEY; compute and storage only. Google Earth Engine would simplify but its free tier is non-commercial only (Phase 0 flag), so avoid.
seeds.who_already_knows: Major outages are usually disclosed by 8-K or press within days and tracked by IIR Energy and Wood Mackenzie Genscape (refinery/power monitoring), so the headline on/off state is largely known; the under-covered gap is the duration of partial run-rates at small-cap single-site names. Macro use is LITERATURE (Henderson, Storeygard and Weil, AER 2012); plant-level equity use: UNKNOWN.
seeds.vendors_selling_similar: Wood Mackenzie Genscape (refinery and power plant monitoring), IIR Energy (outage database); SpaceKnow markets satellite activity indices (REASONED on exact coverage)
seeds.why_ours_differs: Free daily 375-500 m thermal and radiance is enough to measure site-days-active at a named plant, and we target sub-$5B single-site names where vendor monitoring is thin, rather than the refinery complexes Genscape already covers.
seeds.falsifiable_hypothesis: A negative change of more than 10% in cloud-free site-days-active (VIIRS radiance and FIRMS detections over the plant polygon) versus the same quarter a year earlier, measured 20 days before the earnings release, predicts a negative revenue surprise and negative T-1 to T+2 abnormal return for single-site process companies, controlling for consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
seeds.industry_context: Smelters, mills and refineries run around the clock and cannot be throttled cheaply, so volume is nearly binary at the line level and a single outage can erase a quarter's profit. Because fixed costs dominate, days of downtime hit margin more than revenue.
seeds.strongest_reason_wrong: Outages are disclosed and priced quickly; cloud, snow and moonlight contaminate radiance; 500 m pixels mix the plant with neighbours; and the signal is rare and binary, so few events survive to backtest.
seeds.seed_item_extended: [physical] Night-time light intensity (NASA VIIRS) and thermal imagery of plants, smelters, refineries

vet.changes_made: (1) Drop refiners (PBF, DK) from the target list: Wood Mackenzie Genscape's Refinery Stream Monitor and Kayrros already sell refinery activity to desks, so that slice is crowdedness 1-2. (2) Lead with thermal detections (FIRMS VIIRS 375 m, static/industrial source types; EOG VNF if ever reachable) rather than Black Marble radiance: the plant-level literature (Elvidge 2023) is built on infrared emitters, and radiance is contaminated by moonlight, snow and neighbours at 500 m. (3) Restrict to EAF/blast-furnace, smelter, coke, kiln and cracker sites of sub-$5B names with 1-3 dominant sites (CENX, CLF, SXC, OLN, TROX, LXU, EXP and similar). (4) Reframe the target: the headline on/off state is disclosed by 8-K/press and priced, so the hypothesis must test only quarters where the measured site-days-active drop was NOT preceded by a disclosure before the measurement date, and otherwise treat the series as a duration estimator for disclosed outages. (5) First step is a feasibility count: distinct cloud-free detections per site per quarter over 2019-2025; if the median is below ~20 detections per site per quarter, stop. (6) Lower signal_noise from 3 to 2 because the series is close to binary and the event count will be small.

vet.red_team: The equity-relevant event (a line down) is almost always disclosed by 8-K or press within days and sits in consensus by T-1; what remains measurable at 375-500 m (partial run-rates) is contaminated by cloud, snow, moonlight and neighbouring sources. The plant-level literature shows cross-sectional output levels, not within-plant quarterly changes. With ~40 names and rare undisclosed outages, a backtest will have perhaps 10-20 usable quarters, so any coefficient is fragile and the polygon list is easy to overfit.

seeds.name: Sentinel-5P NO2/CH4 columns and VIIRS flaring over named facilities and basins
seeds.sector_focus: Energy and materials: shale E&Ps (Permian, Bakken), refiners, integrated steel, nitrogen and petrochemical plants
seeds.mechanism: Combustion at a refinery, steel mill or ammonia plant emits NO2 in proportion to fuel burned, and TROPOMI resolves large point sources daily at 3.5 x 5.5 km (LITERATURE: Beirle et al., Science Advances 2019, 'Pinpointing nitrogen oxide emissions from space'); a quarter of lower NO2 over the site means lower throughput and revenue. Upstream, VIIRS-detected flaring and Carbon Mapper methane plumes in a producer's acreage rise when gas takeaway is constrained, flagging curtailed oil production or wasted-gas costs that hit the quarter's volumes and lease operating margin.
seeds.measurement_window: Daily S5P and VIIRS passes with ~1 day latency; site-level NO2 must be aggregated over the quarter (clouds, wind) so the quarter reading is final about 3 days after quarter end, 20-40 days before the release. Carbon Mapper plumes are event-based with irregular revisit, so they flag incidents rather than throughput.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~8%: about 100 names in E&P, refining, steel, nitrogen and petrochemicals, e.g. Permian Resources (PR), Matador (MTDR), Civitas (CIVI), Chord (CHRD), PBF Energy (PBF), CVR Energy (CVI), Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF), CF Industries (CF), Olin (OLN)

seeds.cost: $0: free CDSE account and OAuth client, free FIRMS key; Sentinel Hub Statistical API has a free processing-unit quota on CDSE (REASONED). Compute for per-site daily aggregation is modest.
seeds.who_already_knows: Refinery throughput is public weekly at PADD level from EIA, and Enverus/state RRC data cover producer volumes with a 2-3 month lag, so consensus is well anchored for refiners; Kayrros sells methane and flaring intelligence to funds. The gap is company-specific run-rate at steel, nitrogen and chemical sites, which few equity investors measure (REASONED).
seeds.vendors_selling_similar: Kayrros (methane, flaring, energy infrastructure monitoring); Carbon Mapper is public; Enverus for producer volumes
seeds.why_ours_differs: Apply the free daily TROPOMI NO2 column to a fixed list of mid-cap steel, nitrogen and chemical plants rather than the oil and gas basins vendors cover, and use Carbon Mapper plumes as a free incident flag for E&P acreage.
seeds.falsifiable_hypothesis: A negative change of 1 standard deviation in the quarter's cloud-screened, wind-adjusted mean NO2 column over a company's plant polygons versus the trailing four-quarter mean, measured 20 days before the earnings release, predicts a negative revenue surprise and negative T-1 to T+2 abnormal return for single-site process companies, controlling for consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
seeds.industry_context: Furnaces, reformers and crackers burn gas continuously, so the site's NO2 plume is a rough fuel meter; shale producers flare when pipelines are full, so flaring marks takeaway bottlenecks that cap oil output. Both are physical traces of volume that the companies report only at quarter end.
seeds.strongest_reason_wrong: A 3.5 x 5.5 km pixel over an industrial corridor mixes several plants, roads and power stations, and weather drives most day-to-day variance; by the time a quarter of data is averaged, the company's volumes are usually inferable from public EIA, rail and pricing data.
seeds.seed_item_extended: [physical] Flaring and emissions from Sentinel-5P (methane, NO2) as output proxies for oil, steel, chemicals

vet.reject_reason: Three independent kills. (a) Resolution and detection limit: Beirle et al. resolve point sources only after wind-field divergence processing and long averaging, with a detection limit of 0.03-0.11 kg/s NOx (roughly 1,000-3,500 t/yr), and the newer TROPOMI NO2 validation covers 18 large power plants; the steel-plant literature uses CO, not NO2. A single quarter of clear-sky overpasses over one mid-cap plant in an industrial corridor cannot separate the plant's throughput change from wind, boundary-layer and neighbour variance. (b) Legal: Carbon Mapper's current terms (January 2026) grant a non-commercial licence only and prohibit commercial use without a separate agreement, so the E&P incident flag is AMBER and must be dropped. (c) Crowding: flaring and basin methane are Kayrros' core product, and steel volumes are anchored weekly by public AISI production data, so the residual gap is small. The free FIRMS thermal component is folded into S02.

seeds.name: AIS vessel calls at single-company bulk, LNG and fertilizer terminals
seeds.sector_focus: Energy, materials, marine transport: coal and met-coal exporters, LNG and FSRU operators, phosphate and salt shippers, Jones Act and tanker owners
seeds.mechanism: At a terminal owned or exclusively used by one company, each loaded vessel departure is a shipment, so counting calls and draft changes over the quarter nowcasts tons shipped and therefore revenue. The chain holds for exporters with dedicated docks (CONSOL Marine Terminal in Baltimore, Dominion Terminal Associates, Mosaic's Tampa berths, FSRU regas sites) and for shipowners whose fleet utilisation is visible; it fails where terminals are shared by many shippers.
seeds.measurement_window: With a live feed, the quarter's call count is final the day after quarter end, 20-40 days before the release. TESTED HERE: NOAA MarineCadastre daily AIS has the full 2024 year posted but no 2025 files as of 2026-11-11, so the free government archive lags about a year and serves backtests only.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~2%: about 25 names, e.g. Core Natural Resources (CNR), Alpha Metallurgical (AMR), Warrior Met Coal (HCC), New Fortress Energy (NFE), Excelerate (EE), Mosaic (MOS), Compass Minerals (CMP), Kirby (KEX), Matson (MATX), International Seaways (INSW)

seeds.who_already_knows: Kpler and Vortexa sell cargo-level tracking for crude, products, LNG and dry bulk to most energy desks, and EIA weekly coal export estimates plus rail carloads anchor coal consensus; so LNG and crude flows are crowdedness 1-2. Niche single-company met-coal, salt and phosphate berths are less covered (REASONED).
seeds.vendors_selling_similar: Kpler, Vortexa (cargo tracking); Spire (AIS data); MarineTraffic, VesselFinder (vessel APIs)
seeds.why_ours_differs: Restrict to a handful of exclusive-use berths where a ship count is a shipment count, which vendors treat as a footnote to their global flow products, and use the free NOAA archive to validate before paying for live data.
seeds.falsifiable_hypothesis: A positive change of 10% or more in loaded-vessel departures (count, draft-weighted) from a company's exclusive terminal over the fiscal quarter versus the prior quarter, measured 15 days before the earnings release, predicts a positive revenue surprise and positive T-1 to T+2 abnormal return, controlling for consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
seeds.industry_context: Bulk exporters and LNG operators sell in shiploads, so quarterly volume is a small integer count of vessels, each worth tens of millions of dollars. AIS broadcasts every large vessel's position publicly, which is why ship tracking became the standard alternative-data tool for commodity trading.
seeds.strongest_reason_wrong: Companies pre-announce shipped tons and the energy-flow vendors already count the vessels, so the free version is backtest-only and the live version is paid and crowded; draft-based cargo inference is noisy for partial loads.
seeds.seed_item_extended: [physical] AIS ship tracking: vessel queues at single-company ports, LNG terminals, and mining export docks

seeds.name: Catalogued mine and quarry blast counts (USGS ComCat)
seeds.sector_focus: Materials and energy: Powder River Basin and Western surface coal, open-pit metals, aggregates and cement quarries
seeds.mechanism: Surface mines remove overburden with cast blasts large enough (M2+) that regional seismic networks catalogue them as 'mining explosion' or 'quarry blast'; blast frequency and magnitude over a quarter track overburden moved, which leads coal or ore exposed and shipped by weeks. For companies whose output is concentrated in a few large surface mines, a drop in catalogued blasts signals lower production volumes and a revenue miss, and a surge signals pre-stripping for higher next-quarter output.
seeds.measurement_window: ComCat events are reviewed and posted within hours to days, so the full-quarter blast count per mine polygon is final about 3 days after quarter end, 25-40 days before the release. TESTED HERE: Q3-2025 query over a Powder River Basin box returned 48 'mining explosion' events (M2.3-3.5, NEIC 'us' network); a Utah/Nevada box returned 29 quarry/mining events (M0.6-3.4), so the catalogue only captures the largest blasts.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~2%: about 20-25 names, strongest for PRB coal, e.g. Peabody (BTU), Core Natural Resources (CNR), Alpha Metallurgical (AMR), Eagle Materials (EXP), Knife River (KNF), Arcosa (ACA), US Lime (USLM), MP Materials (MP), Coeur (CDE), SSR Mining (SSRM)

But PRB coal consensus already uses EIA's weekly coal production estimates (derived from rail carloads) and MSHA quarterly production, so the gap is mine-level attribution and timing within the quarter, not the industry total.

seeds.falsifiable_hypothesis: A negative change of 25% or more in catalogued blast count (M>=2.3) within a company's mine polygons over the fiscal quarter versus the trailing four-quarter mean, measured 20 days before the earnings release, predicts a negative revenue/production surprise and negative T-1 to T+2 abnormal return for surface-mining companies, controlling for consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
seeds.industry_context: Powder River Basin mines strip tens of metres of overburden with huge cast blasts before draglines and shovels reach the coal seam, and the largest aggregates quarries do the same for rock. The seismic network built to locate earthquakes records these shots as a free, public by-product.
seeds.strongest_reason_wrong: Only blasts above roughly M2.3 are catalogued, giving perhaps 5-15 events per mine per quarter, so counts are noisy and sensitive to network changes; shipments depend on rail availability and customer stockpiles more than on stripping; and PRB volumes are already visible in weekly carloads.
seeds.seed_item_extended: [physical] Public seismometer networks picking up quarry and mine blasting frequency

vet.reject_reason: The catalogue is far too sparse: TESTED HERE the whole Powder River Basin box returned 48 'mining explosion' events in Q3-2025 across roughly a dozen mines, i.e. about 4 catalogued blasts per mine per quarter, so Poisson noise alone is ~50% of the count and any 25% threshold is indistinguishable from chance. Catalogue completeness depends on network configuration and analyst labelling practice, which change over time. The physical chain is also loose: cast blasting removes overburden weeks to months ahead of coal exposure, while shipped tons are set by rail availability and utility stockpiles, and PRB volumes are already visible in EIA's weekly coal production estimates and MSHA quarterly mine-level data. No vendor or paper on blast counts as a production proxy was found; the literature is on discriminating blasts from earthquakes. A custom sub-M2 waveform detector on IRIS data is technically possible and uncrowded, but it is a substantial signal-processing project for ~10 names whose volumes are already public weekly, so it is not worth the effort now.

Pure and Applied Geophysics (2024), seismic blast/earthquake discrimination article (Utah catalogue review of 2,199 events; neural-network classification) - https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00024-024-03440-0

seeds.name: Weekly rail carloads by commodity and DOT truck counts near distribution centres
seeds.sector_focus: Industrials and materials: coal, chemicals, forest products, metals, grain and ethanol shippers; railcar lessors; intermodal and truckload carriers
seeds.mechanism: Class I railroads report weekly carloads by commodity group, and shippers' volumes are a near-linear function of those carloads for commodities moved mostly by rail (coal, chemicals, grain, lumber, scrap, crushed stone); summing the quarter's weeks nowcasts the shipper's volume and revenue, while intermodal counts nowcast truckload and intermodal carriers' loads. Truck counts at a DOT continuous-count station adjacent to a company's distribution centre do the same for that one facility, but mapping is laborious and few stations sit next to a single-tenant DC.
seeds.measurement_window: AAR weekly data are released each Wednesday for the prior week, so the quarter's last week is available about 5 days after quarter end, 20-40 days before the release; STB EP724 carrier service data are weekly too. TESTED HERE: the FHWA TMAS directory lists monthly 2025 continuous-count files but nothing for 2026 as of 2026-11-11, so TMAS lags too far for a nowcast; Caltrans PeMS (free account) is near-real-time with truck classification at some stations (REASONED).

seeds.name: Regulatory exhaust of industrial water and power use (NPDES discharge flows, CEMS heat input, EIA-923 cogeneration)
seeds.sector_focus: Materials, energy and paper: refineries, chemical and chlor-alkali plants, pulp and paper mills, aluminum and steel mills, nitrogen and ethanol plants
seeds.mechanism: Customer-level utility usage is confidential, but the same plants must report cooling-water discharge flow monthly under their NPDES permit (ECHO DMRs) and hourly boiler heat input under EPA's emissions programs (CAMPD CEMS), and industrial cogeneration units report fuel and generation on EIA-923. Each scales with plant throughput, so a quarter of lower heat input or discharge flow at a company's main site implies lower volumes and a revenue and margin miss.

vet.changes_made: (1) The candidate's timing claim is wrong in the right direction: TESTED HERE the ECHO effluent chart for TX0002798 (Bayer Baytown) shows 'Flow, in conduit or thru treatment plant' for the monitoring period ending 30-SEP-26 with ValueReceivedDate 19-OCT-26, a 19-day lag (the earlier '31-MAY-26' reading came from sorting DD-MON-YY strings as if they were MM/DD/YYYY). So the full fiscal quarter of monthly DMR flow is available roughly 20-28 days after quarter end, before most mid-cap releases. Lead the signal with DMR flow and raise lead_time from 5 to 7 days (median), with CAMPD quarterly heat input (Q3-2026 served on 2026-11-11, ~41 days after quarter end, TESTED HERE) as secondary confirmation for companies reporting after ~day 42. (3) Drop EIA-923 except for backfill (2-3 month lag). (4) Map outfalls explicitly: use only process and cooling-water outfalls and exclude stormwater outfalls; weather-adjust with NOAA NCEI daily temperature and precipitation at the nearest station. (5) The DMR lag is TESTED for one Texas (TCEQ NetDMR) permit only; the first Phase 1 task is to measure ValueReceivedDate minus MonitoringPeriodEndDate for every target site and state and to drop sites whose median lag exceeds 35 days. (6) Point-in-time discipline: backtests must use ValueReceivedDate, not the current ECHO snapshot, or the lag reintroduces look-ahead. (7) Get a free api.data.gov key to lift the DEMO_KEY throttle. seeds.name: River stage, drought and soil-moisture exposure (Mississippi, Rhine, Corn Belt)
seeds.sector_focus: Industrials, materials, consumer staples: inland barge operators, grain and ethanol handlers, fertilizer shippers, ag equipment, crop inputs, US names with Rhine-side European plants
seeds.mechanism: Low Mississippi stages at St. Louis and Memphis force draft and tow-size limits, which spike barge freight rates and widen grain basis; that raises logistics costs for grain, ethanol and fertilizer shippers (margin) while lifting barge operators' pricing. Rhine stages below roughly 80 cm at Kaub trigger low-water surcharges and curtailments for US chemical names' European sites. Drought and soil-moisture deficits in the Corn Belt lower yields and farm income, which cuts next-season ag-equipment and crop-input demand (guidance) and raises irrigation equipment orders.
seeds.measurement_window: Gauges are daily and keyless, so the quarter's low-water days and the drought-monitor area are final the day after quarter end, 25-40 days before the release; the same series read in the pre-earnings window informs next-quarter guidance. SMAP soil moisture is daily with 1-3 day latency; USDA crop progress and the Drought Monitor are weekly.

vet.reject_reason: The information is public in real time and already in consensus by T-1: river stages are front-page news during low-water episodes, USDA's Grain Transportation Report publishes St. Louis barge spot rates every Thursday, Kirby and the chemical companies pre-flag impacts on calls (Kirby flagged low-water delay days in 2023; Covestro declared force majeure at Dormagen in August 2026; BASF quantified its 2018 Rhine hit at about EUR 250m), and sell-side ag and transport analysts (e.g., Evercore ISI sizing the Mississippi at ~20% of Kirby's inland business) update within days. The sign is ambiguous for barge operators (rates up versus lighter loads and delay days: Kirby said low water cut revenue and raised costs in 2013), exposure is a few percent of costs for most shippers, and the drought-to-equipment channel is slow macro that is already in guidance consensus. The gauges remain useful as free control variables in an earnings model but carry no edge.

seeds.name: Local planning approvals for data centres, plants and warehouses
seeds.sector_focus: Industrials, real estate, technology: site-work and electrical contractors, HVAC and power equipment, industrial REITs, listed data-centre and compute operators
seeds.mechanism: Rezonings, special-use permits and site-plan approvals in county and city agendas precede construction starts by months, and construction starts become bookings and backlog for site-work, electrical and mechanical contractors and orders for switchgear, generators and cooling. Counting approved square footage and megawatts per quarter in the jurisdictions where a contractor or equipment maker is dominant nowcasts its book-to-bill and the backlog figure that drives guidance; for data-centre operators, their own approvals signal capacity timelines.
seeds.measurement_window: Minutes and agendas post within days of each meeting, so the quarter's approvals are final within a week of quarter end, 20-40 days before the release; the revenue effect lands 1-4 quarters later, so the reading is about backlog and guidance, not the quarter's revenue.

seeds.name: State WARN notices as a plant-closure and restructuring nowcast
seeds.sector_focus: Cross-sector, strongest for manufacturers, auto suppliers, consumer durables, apparel, retail and healthcare services with large US sites
seeds.mechanism: Employers must give 60 days' notice of mass layoffs or closures (50+ employees), and states publish the notices within days; the affected headcount times average compensation proxies the restructuring charge and the lower run-rate cost base, and closure of a specific plant or DC reveals demand weakness in that segment before the company quantifies it. Where the notice is not already press-released, it moves the quarter's margin (charges) and next quarter's guidance.
seeds.measurement_window: Continuous: notices appear days after filing and up to 60 days before the layoff, so the quarter's aggregate affected headcount per company is final at T-1; relative to the company's own disclosure the lead is 0-60 days. Texas (a large manufacturing state) is blocked from the container.

seeds.name: UCC-1 liens on inventory and receivables as a liquidity-stress flag
seeds.sector_focus: Cross-sector small caps with asset-based lending: retail, restaurants, trucking, consumer durables, industrial distributors
seeds.mechanism: A new UCC-1 financing statement naming a company's operating subsidiary as debtor with 'all assets', inventory or receivables as collateral signals a new or expanded secured facility, which for a stressed small cap precedes higher interest expense, covenant amendments and going-concern language; equipment-specific filings instead signal capex. Terminations and continuations show deleveraging or roll-overs. The reading is the count and collateral type of new filings in the quarter.
seeds.measurement_window: Continuous; filings are indexed within 1-3 days so the quarter's filing set is final at T-1. Coverage caveat: UCC-1s are filed in the debtor's state of organisation, which for most public companies is Delaware (paid search), so the free Florida and California indexes capture only subsidiaries organised there.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~15%: about 200 lower-rated names are plausible targets, but free-state coverage of their debtor entities is nearer 2-3%; examples of the type: Kohl's (KSS), Petco (WOOF), Hertz (HTZ), JetBlue (JBLU), Wolverine (WWW), G-III (GIII), Sleep Number (SNBR)

seeds.name: FDA inspection outcomes and 483s, FCC equipment grants (patents/trademarks as context only)
seeds.sector_focus: Healthcare ex-biotech (single-site medtech, generic and animal-health pharma, CDMOs) and consumer/communications hardware
seeds.mechanism: An OAI inspection classification or a lengthy Form 483 at a company's main plant raises the odds of a warning letter, import alert or shipment hold, which cuts revenue and adds remediation cost over the next 1-3 quarters and often forces a guidance cut; conversely, VAI/NAI clearance of a known problem site removes the overhang. For hardware makers, a new FCC equipment grant under the company's grantee code dates the launch of the next product, which times next-quarter revenue. Patent and trademark filings publish with 6-18 month lags and serve only as product-pipeline context, not a 2-10 day signal.
seeds.measurement_window: FDA Data Dashboard classifications post with a 1-3 month lag (REASONED), so the reading covers inspections closed 1-3 months before the release; the annual 483 observation spreadsheets are fiscal-year files. FCC grants appear on fccid.io the day they are granted, but short-term confidentiality hides many for up to 180 days (REASONED), so the reading is the set of grants visible 10 days before the release.

Wayback is blocked from the container, so no point-in-time reconstruction. The market learns OAI from the warning letter or the company's 8-K/press release, both news events. The FCC half concerns launches already guided and many grants sit under short-term confidentiality (REASONED); patents and trademarks are 6-18 months slow by the candidate's own admission. Redica Systems did not appear in my searches, so its product could not be confirmed.

seeds.name: Foreign subsidiary statutory accounts as a hidden-segment check
seeds.sector_focus: Cross-sector mid-caps with material UK, French or Norwegian subsidiaries: consumer brands, industrial equipment, food, specialty chemicals
seeds.mechanism: Foreign subsidiaries file statutory accounts with revenue, margin, headcount and sometimes customer and segment detail that the US parent consolidates away; when one subsidiary is effectively the parent's European segment, its trend reveals margin erosion, intercompany debt build-up or goodwill impairment risk that the parent's segment note hides. The reading is a structural revaluation input (margin, impairment, guidance), not a nowcast of the quarter being reported, because the accounts arrive 9-21 months after the period they cover.
seeds.measurement_window: Filings arrive continuously; UK private-company accounts are due 9 months after the subsidiary's year end, so a reading taken any time before the release covers the subsidiary's prior fiscal year. There is no event timing; the 30-day lead is nominal.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~25%: about 300 names have UK/FR/NO subsidiaries, but the signal is informative only where one subsidiary approximates a segment (~5%, about 60 names), e.g. Crocs (CROX), Columbia Sportswear (COLM), Hain Celestial (HAIN), Spectrum Brands (SPB), Helen of Troy (HELE), Mattel (MAT), Brunswick (BC), Middleby (MIDD), Belden (BDC), Itron (ITRI), Fresh Del Monte (FDP)

seeds.industry_context: Many US mid-caps run Europe through a single UK or French legal entity that must publish audited accounts, while the parent reports only a consolidated 'international' line. The subsidiary's filing is the only public look inside that line.
seeds.strongest_reason_wrong: The accounts are 9-21 months stale and distorted by transfer pricing and intercompany charges, so they rarely say anything about the quarter being reported, and the market has months to absorb them.

vet.revised_universe_coverage: ~5% nominal (about 60 names where one subsidiary approximates a segment); effectively 0% for the 2-10 day earnings trade because the reading has no event timing.
vet.reject_reason: Fails program requirement (a): the accounts cover a period that ended 9-21 months earlier and say nothing about the quarter being reported or next-quarter guidance; the 30-day lead is admitted to be nominal. The mechanism is also structurally broken: a US parent's UK/French/Norwegian subsidiary is usually a limited-risk distributor or cost-plus service entity whose operating margin is fixed by transfer-pricing policy (REASONED; the search results confirm OECD transfer-pricing, management fees and royalties shape these accounts), so a 300 bp divergence from the parent's segment margin measures tax structure, not operations. No vendor or paper supports the segment-gap signal (UNKNOWN), and any genuine deterioration would already be visible in the parent's own segment note and goodwill-impairment-test language several quarters before the subsidiary accounts land. Legal position is clean (Crown copyright, Licence Ouverte, NLOD), which is the only thing in its favour; could be kept as a non-tradable impairment watchlist, but not as a Phase 1 signal.
vet.red_team: Subsidiary operating margins are set by transfer-pricing policy (limited-risk distributor target margins, cost-plus service fees, royalty charges), so divergence from the parent's reported segment margin is a tax-structure artifact rather than information; and because the accounts arrive 9-21 months after the period, anything real in them has already been in the parent's 10-K segment disclosures and impairment-test commentary for several quarters, leaving nothing for a T-1 to T+2 window.

seeds.name: Clustered open-market insider buying (Form 4) and corporate-jet movements
seeds.sector_focus: Cross-sector; Form 4 applies to all names, jet tracking to the subset owning or leasing aircraft
seeds.mechanism: Multiple insiders buying in the open window after the prior release signals that the current quarter is tracking above internal plans, which predicts a positive surprise or guidance raise at the next release (LITERATURE: Lakonishok and Lee, RFS 2001; Cohen, Malloy and Pomorski, 'Decoding Inside Information', JF 2012, who separate opportunistic from routine trades). Because trading blackouts typically start 2-4 weeks before quarter end (REASONED), the final reading is fixed 30-45 days before the release. Corporate-jet flights to a counterparty's headquarters or an unusual plant site precede M&A announcements or operational problems (REASONED; the Occidental-Omaha 2019 case was widely reported), but that is an M&A event, not an earnings event.
seeds.measurement_window: Form 4: cluster score over the open window (roughly days 2-45 after the prior release), final about 30 days before the next release; EDGAR posts filings within two business days of the trade. Jets: continuous live positions that must be self-archived (adsb.lol is live-only); OpenSky gives historical flights by aircraft under non-commercial terms.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~100% for Form 4 (all ~1,300 names); jets: REASONED 30-40% of mid-caps operate an aircraft findable in the FAA registry, often via an LLC or trust; many enrol in FAA LADD/PIA privacy programs that community feeds may or may not honour

seeds.name: ATS open-requisition count and wording shifts
seeds.sector_focus: Labor-driven growth companies with public ATS boards: software/internet, consumer services, healthcare services, staffing-heavy industrials
seeds.mechanism: Open requisitions on a company's own applicant-tracking board are a real-time read of management's internal demand plan: a firm that expects to hit or beat its quarter keeps hiring into it, while one seeing bookings soften lets reqs lapse and stops posting weeks before it tells the market. For software, internet, consumer-services and healthcare-services companies, a quarter-to-date collapse in open reqs (or a shift from 'build/new product' roles toward 'maintain/restructuring/transformation' roles) maps to next-quarter guidance and current-quarter opex (margin). The requisition count is a direct input to opex, so the margin channel is tighter than the revenue channel. LITERATURE: Gutierrez, Lourie, Nekrasov and Shevlin (Management Science, 2020) report that changes in online job postings predict future sales and earnings news; REASONED that the public-ATS version is a noisier subset of what they used.
seeds.measurement_window: Quarter-to-date daily snapshots of open postings from fiscal-quarter start to T-2; signal = log change in open reqs over the final 8 weeks of the quarter versus the first 5 weeks, plus the share of postings in 'build' versus 'maintain/restructure' keyword classes and region concentration. Final reading at T-2. History: zero at start; must be archived daily from now because ATS APIs expose only current postings (TESTED HERE).
seeds.universe_coverage: ~20-25% (REASONED): roughly 250-320 names that expose a Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby or SmartRecruiters board, concentrated in software/internet, consumer services and healthcare services; Workday-hosted boards (most industrials, retailers, utilities) need a per-tenant endpoint that is UNPROBED. Candidate examples to verify: Duolingo (Greenhouse board returned postings, TESTED HERE), Yelp, Etsy, Peloton, Wayfair.

seeds.cost: $0: all ATS APIs are keyless public endpoints; only storage for daily snapshots. No paid tier needed.
seeds.who_already_knows: Sell-side rarely tracks postings systematically for mid-caps, but LinkUp, Revelio Labs, Lightcast and Thinknum sell daily company-level posting counts to many funds, so the aggregate posting-count factor is largely priced for large caps (REASONED). The gap is in mid-cap names and in the wording/role-mix classification, which vendors expose less granularly. Expect modest residual edge, showing up more in opex guidance than revenue.
seeds.vendors_selling_similar: LinkUp, Revelio Labs, Lightcast, Thinknum (all sell company-level job-posting counts and derived series).
seeds.why_ours_differs: Cheaper ($0 versus vendor contracts), daily rather than weekly/monthly refresh, and more granular: requisition-level IDs let us measure reqs pulled before being filled (freeze proxy) and classify wording (build versus maintain, 'restructuring', 'transformation', 'interim'), which aggregate vendor counts do not expose. Honest caveat: vendors have multi-year history and we have none until archived.
seeds.falsifiable_hypothesis: A decline of 20% or more in a company's open requisitions on its public ATS board over the final 8 weeks of the fiscal quarter, measured 2 trading days before the earnings release, predicts lowered forward guidance and a negative T-1 to T+1 sector-ETF-adjusted abnormal return, controlling for 30-day consensus revisions, sector, size and 12-1 momentum.
seeds.industry_context: Hiring plans are set against internal bookings and pipeline forecasts that management sees weeks before investors do, and requisitions are the cheapest lever to pull when a quarter wobbles. Because ATS boards are public and updated in real time, the posting count leaks that internal view without any disclosure event.
seeds.strongest_reason_wrong: Posting counts are dominated by seasonal and structural hiring patterns (year-end freezes, AI-driven headcount restraint across all of software), so a QTD decline is a sector factor rather than a company signal; vendors already sell the clean version to larger funds, and the remaining mid-cap edge may be smaller than round-trip costs.

A raw count decline is unsigned without this. (4) Add Workday tenants via the POST endpoint only after reading each tenant's careers-site terms; keep iCIMS as AMBER. (5) Lower confidence from 18 to 15 for the no-history problem; the margin/opex-guidance channel stays primary. (6) Vendor differentiation is narrow but real on the program's own test: Lightcast refreshes monthly and Revelio's postings start in 2021 (per their pages), so daily req-level pull/fill is faster and more granular, at $0.

seeds.name: Employee-voice negativity (Reddit/HN) ahead of earnings
seeds.sector_focus: Consumer-facing and tech employers with active employee communities: software, consumer internet, retail, restaurants, healthcare services
seeds.mechanism: Current and former employees post about layoffs, leadership turmoil, missed internal targets and quiet hiring freezes on Reddit (company and industry subreddits) and Hacker News weeks before the facts reach a filing. For firms where line employees see demand directly (retail, restaurants, logistics, SaaS sales teams), a rising share of negative, leadership-focused posts in the 90 days before earnings proxies internal deterioration that feeds revenue and guidance misses. LITERATURE: Green, Huang, Wen and Zhou (Journal of Financial Economics, 2019) find that changes in crowdsourced Glassdoor employer ratings predict earnings surprises and returns; REASONED that Reddit/HN mentions are a noisier, sparser substitute because Glassdoor and Indeed are blocked and ToS-prohibited. This is one of the two permitted sentiment-type ideas.
seeds.measurement_window: Rolling 90-day window ending T-2: count and negativity share of posts/comments mentioning the company as an employer (keywords: layoff, RIF, freeze, PIP, leadership, CEO, reorg) versus the company's trailing 4-quarter baseline. Reddit search returns at most ~1,000 results per query (TESTED HERE), so backfill is limited; HN Algolia has full corpus history with created_at filters (TESTED HERE).
seeds.universe_coverage: ~15% (REASONED): roughly 200 names with enough employee-community volume to score, mainly software/internet, large retailers and restaurant chains, hospital and healthcare-services operators; most industrials, utilities and materials firms have too few posts to measure.

seeds.who_already_knows: Glassdoor-derived ratings are sold by Thinknum and Revelio Labs (REASONED) and have been used by quant funds since the 2019 JFE paper, so the employer-rating effect is largely arbitraged for liquid names. Reddit/HN employee chatter is less systematically harvested but is also sparse and noisy. Sell-side ignores it.
seeds.vendors_selling_similar: Thinknum and Revelio Labs (Glassdoor/Indeed-derived employer review series; REASONED that both sell such series).
seeds.why_ours_differs: Not a cheaper copy of Glassdoor; it is a different, lawful source (Reddit API with a registered app, HN) focused on leadership-complaint and freeze keywords rather than star ratings. Granularity is per post with timestamps, letting us measure spikes within the quarter rather than monthly rating averages.
seeds.falsifiable_hypothesis: A one-standard-deviation rise versus the company's trailing 4-quarter baseline in the negativity share of employee-authored Reddit/HN posts over the 90 days before earnings, measured 2 trading days before the release, predicts a negative EPS surprise and a lower T-1 to T+1 sector-adjusted abnormal return, controlling for consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
seeds.industry_context: Employees learn about missed internal targets, layoffs and leadership churn before investors because those events are operational rather than financial, and anonymous forums are where that knowledge surfaces. The effect is strongest where frontline staff observe demand directly, such as retail floors, restaurants and SaaS sales teams.
seeds.strongest_reason_wrong: Reddit/HN volume is driven by consumer brand salience and news coverage, not operations, so negativity spikes are reactions to already-public events (layoff headlines) and carry no information beyond price; the keyless substitute for Glassdoor may simply be too sparse to score more than a handful of names per quarter.

seeds.name: App-rating velocity and chart rank for app-centric consumer tech
seeds.sector_focus: Consumer internet, mobile games, subscription apps, connected fitness and app-first consumer services (ex-GICS Financials)
seeds.mechanism: For companies whose revenue is a function of active users and in-app subscriptions, the daily rate of new App Store ratings (delta of the cumulative userRatingCount from the iTunes lookup API) and the app's rank in Apple's top-free and top-grossing charts track new-user acquisition and monetization within the quarter. A QTD rating-velocity change versus the prior-year quarter nowcasts bookings growth for subscription apps (Duolingo-type), mobile games (Playtika-type) and dating apps (Grindr/Bumble-type), and a sustained drop in grossing rank nowcasts in-app purchase revenue. REASONED: ratings are a roughly fixed fraction of installs, so their velocity is an install proxy; the grossing chart is a direct if ordinal read of IAP revenue.
seeds.measurement_window: Fiscal quarter start to T-1: daily archived snapshots of (a) cumulative rating count per app (iTunes lookup), (b) daily position in US top-free and top-grossing charts (Apple RSS), (c) new-review flow from the customer-reviews RSS (50 per page, about 10 pages deep, TESTED HERE). Signal = YoY change in QTD rating velocity and average grossing rank. History: none until archived (snapshot endpoints, TESTED HERE); Tranco daily lists are retrievable historically for web-rank context.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~7% (REASONED): about 90 names where an app is the primary revenue channel: e.g., Duolingo, Grindr, Life360, Playtika, Peloton, Bumble (verify market caps at run time; Bumble is near the cap floor).

seeds.who_already_knows: Sensor Tower, data.ai, Apptopia and Similarweb sell modelled downloads, DAU and in-app revenue to essentially every fund covering these names, and sell-side analysts quote those panels in previews, so download trends are heavily priced. Crowdedness 1.
seeds.vendors_selling_similar: Sensor Tower, data.ai, Apptopia, Similarweb (downloads, usage and web traffic at scale).
seeds.why_ours_differs: Only on cost ($0) and one angle vendors publish less: rating velocity is a free, daily, per-app install proxy, and the review-text flow lets us measure complaint spikes (pricing changes, outages) at daily granularity. It is a weaker proxy, not a cheaper copy of the same thing. If backtests show it adds nothing over vendor-implied consensus, drop it.
seeds.falsifiable_hypothesis: A YoY change of at least 15% in QTD App Store rating velocity for the company's primary app, measured 1 trading day before earnings, predicts the sign of the revenue surprise versus consensus and the T-1 to T+1 sector-ETF-adjusted abnormal return, controlling for 30-day consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
seeds.industry_context: App-first consumer companies monetize users through subscriptions and in-app purchases, so user acquisition and chart position within the quarter map almost mechanically to bookings. Because Apple exposes chart rank and cumulative rating counts publicly, a daily archive reconstructs the install curve without a paid panel.
seeds.strongest_reason_wrong: Vendor panels already measure downloads and revenue directly and are in consensus, so rating velocity adds no incremental information; ratings are also distorted by in-app rating prompts that companies toggle, producing spurious spikes unrelated to installs.

seeds.name: HS-code import nowcast (Census) for import-dependent hardgoods
seeds.sector_focus: Importers of finished goods: toys, footwear and apparel brands, small appliances, powersports, furniture, consumer-electronics accessories, HVAC equipment
seeds.mechanism: Companies that import finished goods from Asia book revenue when they sell through, but their inventory and sales plan show up first as customs entries. Monthly US import value and quantity by HS-10 code and origin country (Census FT-900 detail) nowcasts the category's sell-in for months 1-2 of the quarter; for a company that dominates its HS category (toys, powersports, grills, e-bikes), the category series is close to its own inbound shipments. A sharp import build with flat consumer demand signals an inventory overhang (gross-margin risk from markdowns), while an import drop signals revenue shortfall or supplier shifts. Company-level bills of lading (Panjiva/ImportGenius) are the direct version but are paid and vendor-saturated; the HS-level Census series is the cheaper, lawful aggregate version. REASONED throughout.
seeds.measurement_window: Months 1 and 2 of the fiscal quarter only: Census releases a month's detail roughly 5-6 weeks after month end (REASONED from the FT-900 schedule), so for a calendar quarter the February release lands in early April and most companies report late April to May; month 3 arrives after the announcement. Signal = YoY change in category import value and units for months 1-2 versus consensus-implied revenue growth. History: monthly from 2013 via the API (per probe), longer via DataWeb.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~8% (REASONED): about 100 names in toys (Mattel, Hasbro), footwear/apparel brands (Crocs, Deckers, Steve Madden, Columbia), small appliances and hardgoods (SharkNinja, Helen of Troy, YETI), powersports (Polaris, BRP, Fox Factory), furniture (RH, La-Z-Boy), HVAC and tools where imports dominate; verify caps and HS concentration per name.

seeds.who_already_knows: Bills of lading are sold at scale by Panjiva, ImportGenius and Descartes Datamyne and appear in sell-side previews for the largest importers (REASONED). HS-level Census series are public and used by some sell-side consumer analysts, but are rarely mapped to mid-cap tickers at HS-10 granularity; the edge, if any, is in the mapping and in names where one company dominates a narrow HS line.
seeds.vendors_selling_similar: Panjiva (S&P Global), ImportGenius, Descartes Datamyne (bill-of-lading data).
seeds.why_ours_differs: Cheaper and lawful: free government aggregates instead of a paid BoL feed; different granularity: HS-10 by origin country, which also captures supplier-country shifts (China to Vietnam/Mexico) that affect tariff cost and gross margin. Not faster: it is slower and covers only 2 of 3 months, so it should be tested as a margin/inventory signal rather than a precise revenue nowcast.
seeds.falsifiable_hypothesis: A YoY change of at least 15% in months-1-to-2 US import value for the company's dominant HS-10 categories, measured 14 days before the earnings release, predicts the sign of the revenue surprise and the direction of inventory-related gross-margin commentary, controlling for consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
seeds.industry_context: Consumer hardgoods brands outsource manufacturing to Asia and must land inventory 1-3 months before sale, so customs data is a physical leading indicator of what they plan to sell. Because the brands own the goods on arrival, import volume also predicts inventory and markdown risk, not just sales.
seeds.strongest_reason_wrong: HS categories pool many companies, and the Census series lags so much that the market already has retailer commentary, port volumes and vendor BoL counts by the time months 1-2 print; company-specific timing (port congestion, tariff pull-forwards) can break the import-to-revenue link entirely in a given quarter.

seeds.name: Google Trends YoY for single-product consumer small caps
seeds.sector_focus: Single-brand consumer discretionary and staples: beverages, footwear, outdoor gear, beauty, consumer audio
seeds.mechanism: For a company whose revenue is dominated by one consumer brand, search interest for that brand is a direct proxy for purchase intent and sell-through within the quarter. A YoY change in the quarter-to-date average of the Google Trends index (pulled in one request with a fixed anchor term to keep normalization stable) nowcasts revenue growth versus consensus-implied growth; Wikipedia pageviews for the brand article give a licensed (CC0), keyless cross-check. LITERATURE: Da, Engelberg and Gao (Journal of Finance, 2011) show Google search volume captures attention and predicts short-run returns; the revenue-nowcast use is REASONED and widely attempted by sell-side.
seeds.measurement_window: Fiscal quarter start to T-2 (Trends daily data lags about 1-2 days): QTD mean of the brand's daily US search index relative to the same days a year earlier, computed within a single 5-year weekly pull plus a 90-day daily pull to avoid normalization drift. Final reading at T-2. History: Trends back to 2004 weekly (REASONED), Wikimedia pageviews daily from 2015.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~5% (REASONED): roughly 60 names where one brand is more than 60% of revenue: e.g., Crocs, YETI, Celsius, Sonos, e.l.f. Beauty, Vita Coco, Deckers (HOKA and UGG as two terms); verify caps at run time.

Edge, if any, is in less-followed names, disciplined normalization and YoY construction, and combining with pageviews to reduce Trends noise.
seeds.vendors_selling_similar: None sell Google Trends itself; Similarweb sells web-traffic panels that overlap in information. Sell-side publishes Trends charts for free.

seeds.falsifiable_hypothesis: A YoY change of at least 15% in the QTD mean Google Trends index for the company's dominant brand, measured 2 trading days before earnings, predicts the sign of the revenue surprise versus consensus and the T-1 to T+1 sector-adjusted abnormal return, controlling for 30-day consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
seeds.industry_context: Single-brand consumer companies live or die on brand heat, and search is where consumers reveal it before they buy. When one product line is most of revenue, the brand search curve and the revenue curve are tightly coupled, which is not true for diversified companies.
seeds.strongest_reason_wrong: Search interest spikes on news, controversies and marketing campaigns rather than purchases, and because the chart is on every analyst's screen the pre-earnings drift already reflects it; the unofficial pytrends endpoint can also silently change normalization between pulls, creating spurious YoY changes.

seeds.name: Complaint-spike precursor to recalls and warranty charges (NHTSA, CPSC, MAUDE)
seeds.sector_focus: Vehicle, powersports and RV OEMs; auto and powersports suppliers; medical device makers (ex-biotech); consumer durables subject to CPSC
seeds.mechanism: Consumer complaints to NHTSA (by make, model year and component), CPSC incident reports and FDA MAUDE device adverse-event reports accumulate for weeks to months before a recall is announced, and the manufacturer books warranty and recall accruals in the quarter the loss becomes probable and estimable (ASC 450), hitting gross margin and EPS. For OEMs in the universe (Harley-Davidson, Polaris, BRP, Winnebago, Thor, Rivian, Lucid) a 90-day complaint rate per model that is 2-3x the trailing baseline and concentrated in one component predicts elevated recall probability and a margin miss; for device makers (Inspire Medical, Penumbra, iRhythm, Tandem, Glaukos) MAUDE event spikes precede FDA recalls that drive shipment holds and guidance. REASONED: the complaint-to-recall link is mechanical because NHTSA and FDA open investigations off these reports; the link to the earnings move depends on whether the recall or accrual lands inside the quarter.
seeds.measurement_window: Rolling 90-day complaint count per make/model-year (NHTSA), per product (CPSC incident reports) or per device brand (MAUDE) ending T-3, versus the trailing 4-quarter daily baseline; plus flags for an open NHTSA investigation or a new recall posted during the quarter. NHTSA complaints post with a lag of days (REASONED); MAUDE posts monthly with a lag (REASONED). History: NHTSA complaints multi-decade; MAUDE from 1991 (REASONED); CPSC recalls queryable by date range (TESTED HERE).
seeds.universe_coverage: ~6% (REASONED): about 75 names: powersports/RV/auto OEMs (Harley-Davidson, Polaris, BRP, Winnebago, Thor, LCI, Rivian, Lucid), suppliers where a component maps to a supplier (Gentherm, Visteon, Dorman aftermarket), medical device makers (Inspire Medical, Penumbra, iRhythm, Tandem Diabetes, Glaukos, Masimo), CPSC-exposed durables (Peloton, SharkNinja). Verify caps.

seeds.name: Own-site stock-outs and markdown depth (Shopify storefronts, Best Buy API)
seeds.sector_focus: DTC-heavy consumer brands on Shopify-class storefronts; consumer-electronics brands sold through Best Buy
seeds.mechanism: A brand's own storefront exposes, per variant, whether it is purchasable and its current and compare-at price. For DTC-weighted apparel, footwear, beauty and gear brands, a rising share of in-season variants out of stock in weeks 6-13 of the quarter signals sell-through ahead of plan (revenue beat) or supply failure (revenue miss, distinguishable by whether new arrivals are also sold out), while deepening and broadening markdowns (share of variants with compare_at_price above price, and average discount) in the last four weeks signal inventory clearance and a gross-margin miss. For consumer-electronics brands, Best Buy's product API gives availability and sale price at the largest US electronics retailer, nowcasting channel sell-through and promotional intensity. REASONED throughout.
seeds.measurement_window: Daily archived snapshots from fiscal-quarter start to T-1: (a) share of variants with available=false, (b) share of variants discounted and mean discount depth, (c) count of new products added. Signal = QTD change versus the same weeks last year once a year of archive exists; until then, versus the prior quarter. History: none (snapshot endpoints, TESTED HERE); must be archived from day one.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~4% (REASONED): about 50 names: DTC brands whose site serves /products.json (Allbirds confirmed TESTED HERE but likely below the cap floor; candidates to verify: Figs, Warby Parker, Hims & Hers, e.l.f. Beauty, Olaplex, YETI, Oddity) plus CE brands with Best Buy distribution (Sonos, Logitech, Corsair, Arlo; Garmin exceeds the cap ceiling). Storefront platform must be verified per name.

seeds.name: Distributor catalog repricing frequency versus PPI pass-through
seeds.sector_focus: Industrial and MRO distributors; building-products, HVAC, pool and electrical distributors; industrial consumables makers
seeds.mechanism: Distributors earn a spread between supplier cost and list/sell price, and their gross margin in a quarter depends on how quickly and how often they reprice relative to supplier cost inflation or deflation. Counting price changes (frequency, direction, average size) across a fixed basket of SKUs on a distributor's own public catalog (MSC Industrial, Global Industrial, Zoro, DXP-type) during the quarter nowcasts the price contribution to revenue and the direction of gross margin; the BLS PPI for the matching commodity and wholesaling industry provides the cost side. Rising catalog prices with flat PPI implies spread expansion (margin beat); flat catalog prices with rising PPI implies compression. Grainger and Fastenal, the usual targets, exceed the cap ceiling and their sites are bot-blocked from the container anyway. REASONED throughout.
seeds.measurement_window: Catalog version: daily or weekly snapshots of a fixed basket of 500-2,000 SKUs per distributor from quarter start to T-2; signal = share of SKUs repriced, mean price change, and the gap to the BLS PPI for the matching commodity. PPI for the quarter's final month is released about 2 weeks after month end (REASONED), so it is available roughly 10-20 days before most distributor reports and covers the full quarter. History: PPI decades; catalog none until archived.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~3% (REASONED): about 35-40 names: MSC Industrial, Global Industrial, DXP Enterprises, Transcat, Distribution Solutions Group, Core & Main, Hillman, Applied Industrial, WESCO, Watsco, Pool Corp, SiteOne, Boise Cascade, BlueLinx (verify caps at run time).

Catalog-level repricing frequency is not sold by any vendor we know of (UNKNOWN) and is rarely measured systematically; the edge is in the timing and breadth of repricing, which management discloses only qualitatively.
seeds.vendors_selling_similar: None known for distributor catalog repricing (UNKNOWN); price-intelligence vendors such as DataWeave and Profitero serve consumer retail rather than industrial MRO.
seeds.why_ours_differs: Direct SKU-level measurement of the distributor's own repricing behaviour against an industry PPI, which nobody sells; cheaper (free) and more granular than analyst models. Honest caveat: the universe is tiny and several target sites may block scraping (legal/ToS risk 3).
seeds.falsifiable_hypothesis: A positive gap of at least 2 percentage points between a distributor's QTD basket price change and the matching PPI change, measured 2 trading days before earnings, predicts a positive gross-margin surprise and a positive T-1 to T+1 sector-adjusted abnormal return, controlling for consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
seeds.industry_context: Industrial distributors pass supplier price increases through with a lag, and their gross margin expands when they reprice faster than costs rise and compresses when costs fall faster than they cut prices. Because catalogs are public, the repricing behaviour that determines that spread is observable in real time.
seeds.strongest_reason_wrong: List prices on the website are not realized prices (large customers buy on contract), so catalog changes may not move blended margin; PPI pass-through is already modelled by every analyst; and the handful of eligible names makes any backtest statistically weak.
seeds.seed_item_extended: Price-change frequency in B2B and industrial-distributor catalogs

seeds.name: Package-download and repo-activity velocity for open-core developer tools
seeds.sector_focus: Open-core and developer-platform software: observability, databases, CI/CD, API and communications platforms, cloud infrastructure
seeds.mechanism: Consumption-priced developer platforms recognize revenue as customers' usage grows, and usage follows adoption of the client SDKs and agents that developers install. Weekly downloads of the company's official packages (PyPI, npm, Docker Hub pulls, Homebrew installs) and the velocity of GitHub stars, forks, issues opened and median time-to-close on its core repositories track developer adoption and product health within the quarter. For companies like GitLab, Elastic, JFrog, DigitalOcean, Fastly, PagerDuty, Twilio, Braze, Amplitude, UiPath and Dynatrace (verify caps), a QTD YoY acceleration in SDK downloads nowcasts net-new usage, and a rising unresolved-issue backlog signals product friction that precedes churn. REASONED: downloads are a leading, noisy proxy for consumption; most revenue comes from existing customers' expansion, which downloads capture only partially.

seeds.name: Trademark intent-to-use filings and CT-log subdomains as launch precursors
seeds.sector_focus: Consumer products, beverages, restaurants, video games and entertainment, medical devices, consumer electronics
seeds.mechanism: Companies file intent-to-use trademark applications 3-12 months before a product launch and issue TLS certificates for launch subdomains days to weeks before. A cluster of new ITU filings and new certificate names tied to one company signals a launch pipeline that drives next-quarter guidance (new SKUs, menu platforms, game titles, device generations); the absence of filings where a launch was promised signals slippage. This is a forward signal about guidance and the launch quarter's revenue, not a nowcast of the quarter being reported. REASONED throughout; no literature cited.

seeds.measurement_window: Trailing 180-day count of new USPTO applications by owner (TSDR daily updates; bulk daily XML) and trailing 90-day count of newly logged certificate names under the company's domains (crt.sh), both read at T-1; the informative horizon is 1-3 quarters ahead, so the final reading before an earnings date is a stock of pipeline rather than a flow for the quarter. History: USPTO bulk back over a century; certificate transparency logs since about 2013 (REASONED).
seeds.universe_coverage: ~25% of the universe files trademarks regularly, but launches are material to results for perhaps ~10% (REASONED): about 130 names in consumer products, beverages, beauty, restaurants, games, med-tech and consumer electronics.

seeds.name: Website diffs: removed products, softened claims, deleted customer logos
seeds.sector_focus: B2B software and services with customer-logo pages; consumer brands with product catalogs; med-tech and industrial firms with product pages
seeds.mechanism: Companies edit their websites before they disclose: a logo removed from the customers page often means a lost account (churn and a revenue miss for B2B software), a product page removed means a discontinued line (revenue and inventory write-down), and softened performance or regulatory claims can precede legal or regulatory trouble. Diffing daily snapshots of a fixed set of pages per company (customers, products, investor FAQ, careers) against the prior snapshot and flagging deletions converts these edits into dated events ahead of the earnings release. The Wayback Machine is blocked from the container, so history must come from Common Crawl (monthly-ish) and our own daily crawl going forward. REASONED; no literature.

The Wayback availability API works (TESTED HERE) but snapshot content on web.archive.org is blocked.

seeds.name: Unscheduled executive departures (8-K Item 5.02) before earnings; lawful LinkedIn substitute

seeds.name: Supplier-first disclosures: early-reporting suppliers flagging cuts from a major customer
seeds.sector_focus: Customers of small listed suppliers: industrial OEMs, auto and truck OEMs, consumer durables, telecom and cable equipment buyers, med-tech, semis and electronics
seeds.mechanism: Small component makers, contract manufacturers and packaging firms often report 1-4 weeks before their large customers and must disclose material demand changes from any customer above 10% of revenue (ASC 280 major-customer disclosure, often named in the 10-K and inferable in the 10-Q). When an early-reporting supplier says its largest customer cut orders, pushed out a program or is destocking, the customer's own revenue, inventory and guidance for the same quarter are mechanically affected, and the customer's consensus usually has not moved because the supplier is thinly covered. The map from 10-K major-customer notes (next row) identifies which supplier statements matter for which in-universe customer. LITERATURE: Cohen and Frazzini (Journal of Finance, 2008) document slow diffusion of information along customer-supplier links (customer news to supplier price); the reverse direction used here is REASONED and less studied.
seeds.measurement_window: The window between the supplier's earnings release (8-K Item 2.02 plus transcript) and the customer's release, typically 5-25 days; the reading is a classified text event (cut, push-out or destock versus increase) tied to a named or inferred customer, finalized the day the supplier reports. History: 8-K index from 2004 (REASONED), XBRL concentration data from about 2009 (TESTED HERE for frames).
seeds.universe_coverage: ~15% (REASONED): about 200 in-universe companies that appear as a >10% customer in at least one listed supplier's disclosures, concentrated in industrial OEMs (Oshkosh, Polaris, Harley-Davidson), consumer durables, telecom and cable equipment buyers, med-tech and electronics; the supplier side is mostly small caps outside the universe, which is fine because we trade the customer.

seeds.sector_focus: In-universe suppliers whose >10% customers report earlier: auto, truck and aero suppliers, electronics and semicap suppliers, packaging, consumer-product vendors to big-box retailers, telecom equipment
seeds.mechanism: Build a point-in-time map from each in-universe company's XBRL ConcentrationRiskPercentage disclosures and 10-K major-customer notes to the named customer (Walmart, Home Depot, Lowe's, Apple, Boeing, GM, AT&T, Amazon, Costco, Target and similar mega-caps that report early). When the customer reports results or guidance before the supplier, its segment revenue, inventory commentary and capex plans propagate mechanically to the supplier's quarter in proportion to the disclosed revenue share. seeds.name: Index rebalance and forced-flow overlay around earnings dates
seeds.sector_focus: All sectors; most relevant to names near S&P 400/600 and Russell 1000/2000 boundaries and to names with heavy ETF ownership
seeds.mechanism: This is not a fundamental nowcast; it conditions the event trade. Scheduled index events (S&P quarterly rebalances on the third Friday of March, June, September and December; Russell reconstitution in late June, with FTSE Russell's announced move to semi-annual reconstitution from 2026 - REASONED, verify on lseg.com) and ad-hoc S&P additions and deletions create forced buying or selling by index funds that can swamp or amplify the post-earnings move when an earnings date falls inside the rebalance window. Distressed-holder forced selling is observable only indirectly (FINRA short interest, 13D/13F changes, Form 4) and is UNKNOWN as a reliable signal. The practical use is a filter: avoid or size down event trades whose exit window overlaps a known forced-flow date, and note announced deletions where passive selling into the effective date coincides with an earnings release. LITERATURE: index-inclusion price effects (Shleifer 1986; Harris and Gurel 1986; Chen, Noronha and Singal 2004) are well documented and have shrunk over time.
seeds.target: distress (forced-flow conditioning of the abnormal return; not revenue or EPS)

seeds.name: Trade-show footprint changes (booth size, exhibitor presence, event-staff postings)
seeds.sector_focus: Consumer electronics (CES), retail technology (NRF), auto aftermarket (SEMA/AAPEX), medical imaging and devices (RSNA, HIMSS), machine tools (IMTS), firearms and outdoor (SHOT Show), construction equipment (CONEXPO)
seeds.mechanism: For companies whose selling season is anchored to an annual trade show, the booth size listed in the exhibitor directory, presence versus absence, and the count of event and field-marketing roles posted on the company's ATS in the run-up are a budgeted, forward-looking read of marketing spend and product pipeline. A shrinking booth or a skipped show signals SG&A cuts (margin positive) and a thin pipeline (guidance negative); a larger booth with many new-product listings signals launch-driven guidance. The reading is final when the directory is published, typically 1-2 months before the show, which is often weeks before the earnings release that follows the show. REASONED throughout; no literature.
seeds.measurement_window: Per show-year: booth square footage (where listed) and presence flag from the exhibitor directory, compared with the prior year, read when the directory is published (CES around November-December for a January show; NRF around December; others vary), plus ATS postings for events, trade-show and field-marketing roles in the 120 days before the show. History: only the current show's directory is online (TESTED HERE for CES and NRF); past years must come from our own archive or Common Crawl.
seeds.universe_coverage: ~8% (REASONED): about 100 names where one show anchors the sales year: consumer electronics and accessories (Sonos, Logitech, Corsair, Arlo), auto aftermarket (Dorman, Fox Factory, Holley), firearms and outdoor (Sturm Ruger; Smith & Wesson is near the cap floor), med-tech imaging and devices (Masimo, iRhythm), machine tools and welding (Kennametal, Lincoln Electric), construction equipment (Terex, Astec). seeds.falsifiable_hypothesis: A year-over-year reduction of at least 25% in a company's listed booth area (or a skipped anchor show) at its primary trade show, measured at least 30 days before the first earnings release after the show, predicts lowered forward guidance and a negative T-1 to T+2 sector-adjusted abnormal return, controlling for consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
seeds.industry_context: In show-anchored industries the annual show is where the year's orders are written and new products are revealed, so the budget a company commits to it reflects its own expectation for the year. Exhibitor directories publish that commitment months in advance.
seeds.strongest_reason_wrong: Booth decisions are made a year ahead on a marketing budget cycle unrelated to the current quarter, many companies have shifted to private events regardless of outlook, and with one observation per company per year there is no statistical power for a decade.

ideas.name: Texas mixed-beverage gross receipts by location as a same-store alcohol-sales nowcast for restaurant and eatertainment chains
ideas.sector_focus: Casual dining, sports bars, eatertainment (Topgolf, Dave & Buster's, Bowlero/Lucky Strike), sushi/steak chains with Texas footprints
ideas.mechanism: Every Texas establishment holding a mixed-beverage permit must file a monthly gross-receipts tax return (Tax Code ch. 183) itemizing liquor, wine, beer and cover-charge receipts; the Comptroller publishes these location-level dollar amounts on data.texas.gov. For a chain whose alcohol is 10-35% of sales and whose Texas units are 10-25% of the system, same-location YoY alcohol receipts move with traffic and check, so a matched-location index for the quarter's reported months is a cash-basis read on same-store sales before the company reports. Applies to alcohol-heavy restaurant and entertainment chains with company-operated (not franchised) Texas units, where the taxpayer_name field maps cleanly to the parent.
ideas.measurement_window: Monthly location receipts. TESTED HERE 2026-11-11: September 2026 had 22,677 rows filed (complete) while October had 1,900 (~8%), so a month is essentially complete ~40 days after month-end; dataset rowsUpdatedAt 2026-11-07. Months 1-2 of a quarter are complete well before any announcement; month 3 is complete only when the announcement falls >=42 days after quarter-end (Texas Roadhouse, BJ's, Cheesecake, Bloomin' typically yes; Brinker's late-January report gets 2 of 3 months with ~25 days lead).
ideas.universe_coverage: ~2-3%: roughly 25-35 restaurant/leisure names with material Texas company-operated units. Examples (verify cap band): Texas Roadhouse (TXRH), Brinker (EAT), Dave & Buster's (PLAY), BJ's Restaurants (BJRI), Cheesecake Factory (CAKE), Bloomin' Brands (BLMN; 37 Outback locations found in the data), Topgolf Callaway (MODG), Kura Sushi (KRUS), Portillo's (PTLO; 9 TX locations found), Cracker Barrel (CBRL), Lucky Strike/Bowlero (LUCK), Darden (DRI).

ideas.why_ours_differs: Tax-filed dollar receipts at the individual location (not device-sampled visits or a card panel with coverage bias), free, with full company-operated coverage inside Texas; alcohol receipts also carry a mix signal (bar vs. dining occasion) that traffic data cannot see.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: A change of at least +/-3 percentage points in matched-location YoY alcohol receipts (Texas units grouped by taxpayer_name and location_address) over the quarter's filed months, measured 5 days before the earnings release, predicts the sign of the same-store-sales surprise versus consensus and the T-1 to T+1 abnormal return versus XLY, controlling for 30-day consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
ideas.industry_context: Restaurant stocks move on same-store-sales surprises, and alcohol is the highest-margin, most traffic-sensitive line in casual dining and eatertainment. Texas is a top-three state for most of these chains and the only large state that publishes location-level alcohol receipts.
ideas.strongest_reason_wrong: Texas is a regional sample tied to oil-economy and weather idiosyncrasies; alcohol incidence is secularly declining so alcohol receipts can fall while food sales hold; month 3 is often incomplete at announcement; and because the dataset is known, sophisticated holders may already trade it, leaving little post-announcement drift.

alt_records.name: Texas mixed-beverage tax receipts per location as a same-store-sales nowcast for casual dining and eatertainment
alt_records.mechanism: Every Texas mixed-beverage permittee must file a monthly gross-receipts tax return per location, and the Comptroller publishes liquor, wine, beer and total receipts by location, permit and month on the state open-data portal. Alcohol is roughly 10-25% of casual-dining sales and co-moves with traffic and check, so same-location YoY growth in alcohol receipts across a chain's Texas units nowcasts Texas same-store sales for that chain before the quarter is reported. Texas is 8-20% of system units for several listed chains, and the Texas trend extrapolates to Sunbelt peers. The edge is the gap between this tax-filed, location-level growth and the consensus same-store-sales number, which is built from card panels and management commentary. Applies to any company whose Texas units sell alcohol: restaurants, Topgolf-type venues, cinemas, bowling, hotels.
