ideas.name: Pre-launch certification cadence: new FCC grants per grantee code (via fccid.io) with confidentiality-expiry dates, cross-checked against Wi-Fi Alliance certifications, as a SKU-slate and sell-in nowcast for consumer electronics
ideas.sector_focus: Consumer electronics, PC and gaming peripherals, home networking and smart-home hardware
ideas.mechanism: Every RF-emitting consumer device needs an FCC equipment authorization before sale, and most also obtain Wi-Fi Alliance certification. Grants appear under the company's grantee code weeks to months before launch, often with a short-term confidentiality request whose expiry date is the planned launch date. Counting new grants per grantee per trailing 180 days versus the same window a year earlier, and counting confidentiality expiries that fall inside the reported or next quarter, nowcasts the number of new SKUs shipping; retail sell-in precedes launch by 2-6 weeks and new SKUs carry higher margins. A quarter with no new grants where the prior year had several implies a thinner slate and guidance risk. Applies to Logitech, Sonos, Corsair, Arlo, Netgear, Roku, Garmin (if within the cap band), Peloton, Cricut, Ubiquiti, Digi, Impinj. Differently measured from seed 15: counts per grantee with launch-date extraction rather than filing-level reading. ideas.name: Open-crawl tag census: counting customer sites that embed a vendor's client-side snippet across monthly Common Crawl / HTTP Archive snapshots as a net-customer-adds nowcast for SMB SaaS, martech and commerce platforms
ideas.sector_focus: Martech, e-commerce platforms, CX software, SMB SaaS, website builders
ideas.mechanism: Many SaaS platforms require a public JavaScript snippet or hostname on every customer site (Klaviyo static.klaviyo.com, Braze web SDK, Yext pages, LivePerson lpcdn, Sprinklr, Wix static.parastorage.com, BigCommerce cdn11.bigcommerce.com, Global-e checkout, HubSpot js.hs-scripts.com, Amplitude, Zendesk widget). Common Crawl publishes monthly crawls with CDX indexes and byte-range WARC access, and HTTP Archive publishes monthly Wappalyzer technology detections for millions of sites; counting distinct registrable domains carrying a vendor's fingerprint across consecutive months, weighted by Tranco rank, yields gross adds, churn and net adds of live customers, the driver of subscription and GMV-based revenue for SMB-heavy platforms. Applies to Wix, BigCommerce, Klaviyo, Braze, Yext, LivePerson, Sprinklr, Zeta, Global-e, Amplitude, Semrush, Similarweb, GoDaddy. Labels: Common Crawl DATA; HTTP Archive UNPROBED; link to revenue REASONED.
ideas.measurement_window: Three monthly crawls per fiscal quarter; the crawl covering the last month of the quarter is typically released 2-3 weeks after its window (REASONED), giving a full-quarter reading 10-20 days before most prints.
ideas.universe_coverage: ~3%: about 35-40 names in martech, e-commerce platforms, CX software and SMB SaaS. Examples: Wix (WIX), Klaviyo (KVYO), Braze (BRZE), Yext (YEXT), Sprinklr (CXM), Global-e (GLBE), BigCommerce (BIGC, if above the cap floor).

ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: A QoQ change of more than 2% in Tranco-weighted net customer-domain adds for a vendor's snippet, measured 10 days before the earnings date, predicts the sign of the revenue surprise and the T-1 to T+2 abnormal return versus IGV, controlling for consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.

ideas.name: Builder-named municipal permit issuances and final inspections / certificates of occupancy as a quarterly starts-and-closings nowcast for mid-cap homebuilders
ideas.sector_focus: Consumer discretionary (homebuilding), building products, manufactured housing
ideas.mechanism: A homebuilder's quarterly revenue is closings; a closing cannot occur until the municipality records a passed final inspection or issues a certificate of occupancy, so counting final-inspection/CO records whose applicant or contractor field is one of the builder's operating entities (from 10-K Exhibit 21) gives a direct count of homes that became deliverable during the quarter, and permit issuances under the same names count starts that become next quarter's deliveries. The count is lot-level and recorded within days of the event, so the quarter-end tally is final 1-2 weeks after quarter end, before the builder prints 3-5 weeks after quarter end. Applies to production builders with concentrated metro exposure (Texas, Arizona, Florida, Carolinas) and, through them, to installers and distributors billed on closings.
ideas.measurement_window: Full fiscal quarter of final-inspection/CO dates (closings proxy) and permit issue dates (starts proxy), restricted to the city-limit portals actually covered; quarter-end count final about 7 days after quarter end (REASONED from Austin max completed_date = 2026-11-09 on 2026-11-11, TESTED HERE). Census BPS place-level monthly (no builder names) lands ~18 days after month end and covers months 1-2 as a control.
ideas.universe_coverage: ~3%: about 25 names if the builder-named leg works, plus ~10 downstream names. Builders under $30B: Taylor Morrison (TMHC), Meritage (MTH), KB Home (KBH), Tri Pointe (TPH), M/I Homes (MHO), Century Communities (CCS), LGI Homes (LGIH), Beazer (BZH), Dream Finders (DFH), Green Brick (GRBK), Hovnanian (HOV), Toll (TOL), PulteGroup/NVR near the cap; Lennar and D.R. Horton exceed the cap but appear in the data as controls. Downstream: Installed Building Products (IBP), TopBuild (BLD), Builders FirstSource (BLDR); manufactured housing Skyline Champion (SKY), Cavco (CVCO) via Census MHS shipments. Caveat TESTED HERE: inside Austin city limits Taylor Morrison shows only 3-8 finals a month and Dallas city shows ~500 Lennar new-SF permits over 2018-2025, i.e. the big suburban volume sits in county and suburban portals that still have to be added, so honest coverage today is a pilot, not the 25 names.

ideas.cost: $0 (public portals; Socrata app tokens free). Engineering cost is the real cost: one adapter per portal (Socrata, CKAN, ArcGIS Hub/REST, Accela, Tyler) and a fuzzy entity matcher for builder LLC names.
ideas.who_already_knows: Zonda and John Burns Research and Consulting sell field-survey starts and closings to the sell side and to builders (named in the brief; REASONED that they are the consensus input). BuildFax (Verisk) and ATTOM sell aggregated permit data (REASONED, not verified for this use). Sell-side models anchor on the builder's own closings guidance and backlog, mortgage applications and Census new-home sales; builder-entity-level permit/CO counts from municipal portals are not in previews (REASONED). Closings guidance is usually within a few percent, so much of the level is priced; the edge is the deviation versus guidance caused by cancellations and cycle-time slips in the last month of the quarter.
ideas.vendors_selling_similar: Zonda (starts/closings surveys), John Burns Research and Consulting (surveys), BuildFax/Verisk and ATTOM (permit data, REASONED). None of the brief's listed alternative-data vendors (Placer.ai, Earnest, etc.) sell builder-named CO counts.
ideas.why_ours_differs: Daily, lot-level, free and tagged to the builder's own legal entity, versus monthly or quarterly surveyed or modelled counts sold at scale; ours measures finals/COs (deliverability) rather than starts, which is closer to the revenue line; and it can be re-run the morning after quarter end.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: A positive deviation of at least 10% in builder-entity-tagged final-inspection/CO counts over the fiscal quarter (summed across covered portals and scaled by each portal's trailing 4-quarter share of the builder's reported closings) versus the builder's closings guidance midpoint, measured 7 days after quarter end (at least 14 days before the print), predicts a positive closings/revenue surprise and a positive T-1 to T+1 abnormal return versus XHB/ITB, controlling for consensus revisions over the prior 30 days, the 30-year mortgage-rate change, sector, size and momentum.
ideas.industry_context: Production homebuilders recognise revenue when a home closes, and a home cannot close until the local building department passes its final inspection or issues a certificate of occupancy, which it records in its permit system the same day. Builders operate through state-specific subsidiaries (for example 'Taylor Morrison of Texas, Inc.'), whose names appear verbatim in the permit applicant and contractor fields, so public permit portals carry a builder-level ledger of starts and completions.
ideas.strongest_reason_wrong: Coverage: the tested city portals capture a small slice of each builder's metro volume (suburban and county jurisdictions dominate), so the scaled count may be too noisy to beat the builder's own guidance; final inspection is not a closing (spec homes can pass final and sit unsold for months), and builders already publish backlog and guidance that embed the same cycle-time information, so the residual may be a proxy for regional demand already priced via mortgage rates and peer prints.

ideas.name: FDA drug-shortage list status transitions and competitor first-generic/ANDA approvals (openFDA) as a product-level volume and price nowcast for injectable and specialty generic manufacturers
ideas.sector_focus: Healthcare ex-biotech: generic injectables, specialty generics, 503B outsourcing, hospital pharmacy suppliers
ideas.mechanism: For a generic injectable, quarterly revenue is set by how many competitors can supply the molecule-presentation: when a rival's presentation enters the FDA drug-shortage list as 'Currently in Shortage' or 'Available / limited', the remaining suppliers absorb hospital demand at higher net prices for the weeks the status persists; when a competitor's ANDA or a first generic is approved against a company's product, share and price fall from the launch date. Both events are dated, product-specific and public the day they happen, so summing shortage-days (weighted by the company's share of listed presentations of that molecule) and launch-days across the quarter gives a nowcast of the quarter's volume and price mix. Applies to companies whose revenue is concentrated in a few dozen hospital injectables or specialty generics.
ideas.measurement_window: Full fiscal quarter of daily shortage-status and approval events; the quarter-end reading is final the day after quarter end, and the companies print 5-6 weeks later. CMS ASP quarterly files (published ~6-8 weeks before the effective quarter, REASONED) give next-quarter Part B reimbursement per HCPCS code as a forward price leg.
ideas.universe_coverage: ~1.5%: about 15-20 names, e.g. Amphastar (AMPH), ANI Pharmaceuticals (ANIP), Amneal (AMRX), Harrow (HROW), Perrigo (PRGO, Rx/OTC generics), Prestige (PBH, consumer; weak fit), plus hospital-supply and 503B names that gain from shortages (e.g. compounding exposure at Harrow) and larger foreign-listed generics as controls. Buyers of shortage drugs (hospital operators, Owens & Minor) are second-order.

ideas.who_already_knows: IQVIA (weekly scripts/NSP) and Symphony Health are the sell-side volume inputs; both cover hospital injectables poorly (REASONED, as the brief states). ASHP/University of Utah maintain a separate shortage list used by hospital pharmacists; Vizient publishes shortage commentary. Specialist analysts watch the headline shortages (e.g. GLP-1, IV fluids) but do not systematically score each company's molecule-level exposure (REASONED). Management often flags shortage-driven upside on the prior call, so part of a persisting shortage is priced; new entries and exits in the last six weeks of a quarter are the least priced.
ideas.vendors_selling_similar: IQVIA and Symphony Health (ICON) sell prescription and hospital purchase data at scale; neither sells a shortage-exposure index. No listed alternative-data vendor sells this.
ideas.why_ours_differs: Free, daily, product- and company-specific regulatory exhaust that is causally upstream of the IQVIA volume number, available the day of the status change rather than weeks later, and buildable as a point-in-time panel by snapshotting.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: An increase of at least 45 competitor shortage-days in the fiscal quarter (summed over molecule-presentations where the company holds at least 20% of listed NDC presentations, net of the company's own shortage-days), measured 5 days after quarter end (at least 25 days before the print), predicts a revenue surprise of at least +2% versus final consensus and a positive T-1 to T+1 abnormal return versus XLV; a first-generic or additional ANDA approval against a product that is at least 10% of the company's revenue, launched at least 30 days before quarter end, predicts the opposite, controlling for consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
ideas.industry_context: Hospital injectables are commodity products supplied by two to five manufacturers each, with thin margins and frequent plant-quality disruptions; when one supplier drops out, the others sell every vial they can make at higher spot prices until the FDA lists the shortage as resolved. Generic entry works in reverse: the first additional approval on a specialty generic typically cuts price by 30-60% within two quarters (REASONED), so the dates of approvals and shortage transitions set the quarter's mix.
ideas.strongest_reason_wrong: Shortage-driven upside is capacity-limited (the beneficiary may already be running flat out, so status changes add price not volume) and management guides for it; the FDA list lags real supply conditions by weeks and 'Available' entries persist for years, so a naive shortage-days count is noisy; and the companies in the universe each have dozens of products, so one molecule rarely moves the quarter by more than consensus dispersion.

ideas.industry_context: Shale wells produce most of their first-year output in the first months after they are turned in line, so a quarter's production is dominated by how many wells came online and how early; operators guide TIL counts but slip them with crew availability and weather. ideas.name: Interstate pipeline informational postings: daily scheduled quantities at single-plant delivery meters as a gas-input run-rate nowcast for nitrogen, methanol, gas-fed chemical, gas-processing and LNG names
ideas.sector_focus: Materials and energy: nitrogen fertilizer, methanol, gas-fed chemicals, midstream processors, LNG export, merchant gas-fired generation
ideas.mechanism: Under 18 CFR 284.13 and NAESB WGQ standards every interstate pipeline posts, daily, the scheduled and operationally available quantity at each receipt and delivery point; for a plant fed by a single pipeline meter (an ammonia complex, a methanol plant, a gas processing plant's fuel/residue point, an LNG train's feed-gas meter), the scheduled delivery is the plant's gas consumption that day, which for a nitrogen or methanol plant is proportional to output and for an LNG exporter is proportional to cargoes. Summing the quarter's daily deliveries versus the plant's nameplate and the trailing year gives utilisation, and gaps of several days reveal unplanned outages before management discloses them. Applies to companies whose EBITDA depends on one to three large gas-fed sites.
ideas.measurement_window: Full fiscal quarter of gas days; the reading is final the day after quarter end (postings are made for the next gas day and revised intraday, REASONED); single-plant chemical and fertilizer names print 4-6 weeks after quarter end. History retention per EBB is UNKNOWN; some EBBs allow date-range queries back several years (REASONED).
ideas.universe_coverage: ~1.5%: about 15-20 names. ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: A deviation of at least 5% in the quarter's summed scheduled deliveries at a plant's delivery meter(s) versus the trailing 4-quarter average adjusted for announced turnarounds, measured 3 days after quarter end (at least 20 days before the print), predicts a same-sign production-volume and revenue surprise versus consensus and a same-sign T-1 to T+1 abnormal return versus XLB (or AMLP for processors), controlling for the quarter's benchmark product price change (Tampa ammonia, US Gulf methanol), consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
ideas.industry_context: Ammonia and methanol plants convert pipeline natural gas into product at a nearly fixed ratio (roughly 32-34 MMBtu per tonne of ammonia, REASONED), so gas delivered to the plant is output; unplanned outages at a single complex can remove 10-20% of a quarter's volume for a one- or two-plant company. Interstate pipelines are required by FERC to post scheduled quantities at every point so that shippers can see available capacity, which makes the plant's daily gas intake public.
ideas.strongest_reason_wrong: Many large plants sit on intrastate pipelines or have two or three supply meters (some behind LDCs) that are not posted, so the mapping may be incomplete and the ratio to output unstable; postings can be aggregated or masked for confidentiality at some points; and for CF the market already prices outages because the company and trade press (Argus, CRU) report them within days, leaving little residual by the print.

ideas.name: AD/CVD determination calendar and duty-rate magnitude from the Federal Register API, paired with Census import unit values, as an in-quarter pricing and import-competition signal for domestic metals, building-products and chemicals producers
ideas.sector_focus: Materials and industrials: steel products, aluminum extrusions, wood cabinets, tires, lumber, titanium dioxide and other chemicals
ideas.mechanism: Commerce's preliminary and final AD/CVD determinations set cash-deposit rates on named exporters from the publication date, and critical-circumstances findings make them retroactive 90 days; importers stop ordering or re-price within weeks, and the domestic producer's spot price and order book move inside the quarter in which the determination lands. The direction is known once the case calendar is published, but the rate magnitude (which can be 5% or 300%) and the import-volume and unit-value response in the quarter are not, and both are observable: the rate from the Federal Register notice and the response from Census monthly HS imports. Applies to domestic producers with a large share of sales in a covered product and to listed importers or distributors of the same product.
ideas.measurement_window: Determination notices are dated events within the quarter (the Federal Register notice is final the day it publishes); the import-volume response comes from Census HS data with a ~6-week lag, so before the print it covers months 1-2 of the quarter. Lead time is the gap between the last relevant notice and the print, typically 2-8 weeks.
ideas.universe_coverage: ~6%: about 75-90 names. Steel and aluminum: Insteel (IIIN), Northwest Pipe (NWPI), Century Aluminum (CENX), Kaiser (KALU), Constellium (CSTM), Olympic Steel (ZEUS), Ryerson (RYI), TimkenSteel/Metallus (MTUS), Commercial Metals (CMC), Steel Dynamics (STLD), Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF), Worthington Steel (WS), Atkore (ATKR), Mueller (MLI); building products: American Woodmark (AMWD), MasterBrand (MBC), JELD-WEN (JELD), Louisiana-Pacific (LPX), Boise Cascade (BCC), UFP (UFPI), Quanex (NX), Mohawk (MHK); tires: Goodyear (GT); chemicals: Tronox (TROX), Kronos (KRO), Chemours (CC); paper: Clearwater (CLW); solar: Array (ARRY), Shoals (SHLS), First Solar near the cap; mattresses: Sleep Number (SNBR), Tempur Sealy (TPX).

ideas.cost: $0 (Federal Register API keyless; Census key free; USITC DataWeb account free).
ideas.who_already_knows: Trade lawyers, the petitioning producers and their sell-side analysts follow each case, and the headline outcome (affirmative/negative) is in consensus by the time the schedule is published; Panjiva/ImportGenius users see import volumes with a few weeks' lag. What is not modelled is the cross-section: dozens of simultaneous cases with rates that surprise by tens of points, and the Census unit-value response in the quarter, which analysts cite qualitatively rather than quantify (REASONED). Priced-in share is high for the direction, low for magnitude and timing.
ideas.vendors_selling_similar: Panjiva (S&P Global) and ImportGenius sell bill-of-lading import data; no vendor is known to sell an AD/CVD determination-magnitude event panel for equities (UNKNOWN).
ideas.why_ours_differs: Event-level duty-rate magnitudes parsed from the Federal Register full text, joined to the company's covered-product share and to Census unit values, built as a scheduled-event panel rather than qualitative commentary; keyless and same-day.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: A preliminary or final AD/CVD cash-deposit rate that is at least 20 percentage points above the preceding stage's rate (or the petition's alleged margin for a preliminary determination), or an affirmative critical-circumstances finding, published in the 60 days before the print on a product that is at least 30% of a domestic producer's revenue, predicts a positive EPS surprise versus final consensus and a positive T-1 to T+1 abnormal return versus XLB/XLI for the producer, and the opposite for listed importers of the product, controlling for consensus revisions over the same 60 days, the relevant commodity price change, sector, size and momentum.
ideas.industry_context: Antidumping and countervailing duties are imposed product-by-product and country-by-country after a petition by domestic producers; Commerce sets the rate in scheduled preliminary and final determinations and CBP collects cash deposits from the publication date, so imports of the covered product often fall sharply and domestic prices rise within the same quarter. Rates vary enormously (single digits to several hundred percent) and the petitioners' public guidance rarely quantifies the effect on their own quarter.
ideas.strongest_reason_wrong: The schedule and the petitioners' arguments are public for months, so the equity reaction happens on the determination day, not at earnings; the within-quarter revenue effect is diluted by contracts and inventories; and the cross-section of affected mid-caps is small for any one case, so the signal is a handful of events a year.
ideas.canonical_name: AD/CVD determination calendar and duty-rate magnitude from the Federal Register API, paired with Census import unit values, as an in-quarter pricing and import-competition signal for domestic metals, building-products and chemicals producers

ideas.sector_focus: Consumer discretionary hardgoods (boats, outboards, motorcycles, golf), industrial equipment dealers and rental
ideas.mechanism: Japan publishes provisional export values and quantities by 9-digit HS line and destination country about 20 days after month end, with a first-20-days flash around day 10, far ahead of US Census import data; for product lines where Japan is the dominant origin and the US buyer or competitor is a listed mid-cap, the export series is a direct sell-in measure for the quarter. Examples: HS 8407.21 outboard motors (Yamaha, Honda, Suzuki, Tohatsu ship to US boat builders and dealers), HS 8711 motorcycles (Honda, Kawasaki, Yamaha, Suzuki versus Harley-Davidson and Polaris), HS 9506.31 golf clubs (Srixon, Bridgestone, Mizuno versus Acushnet and Topgolf Callaway), HS 8429.52 excavators and HS 8701.9x tractors (Komatsu, Hitachi, Kubota into rental fleets and dealers). Rising outboard exports mean boat builders are taking engines for current production; rising Japanese motorcycle or club exports mean more competing supply and promotional pressure for the US brand.
ideas.measurement_window: Three calendar months of the US company's fiscal quarter; month 3 provisional by HS line is available ~20 days after quarter end (REASONED from Japan customs release calendar; TESTED HERE: 'October 2026 first 20 days provisional' XML published 2026-11-10), and most target companies print 4-6 weeks after quarter end. ideas.sector_focus: Industrials (truckload, LTL and logistics with Mexico cross-border lanes) and consumer discretionary (auto suppliers with Mexican plants)
ideas.mechanism: US-Mexico freight for Laredo-centric carriers is a direct function of northbound loaded trucks and containers crossing at Laredo, Otay Mesa, El Paso, Nogales and Pharr, which CBP counts and BTS publishes monthly by port and measure; a carrier with 10-20% of revenue on those lanes sees its cross-border loads move with the port counts. Upstream, INEGI's registry of light-vehicle production by plant and model (published ~5 business days after month end) tells which Mexican assembly plants ran harder, and a supplier whose 10-K places its main plants next to those assembly plants (e.g. seat, axle, thermal and electronics makers in Saltillo, Silao, San Luis Potosi, Aguascalientes, Hermosillo) sells into that production in the same month. The two series together nowcast cross-border revenue for carriers and plant-level volume for suppliers.
ideas.measurement_window: BTS: monthly, ~6-week lag (TESTED HERE: September 2026 rows present on 2026-11-11), so months 1-2 of the quarter are available 2-3 weeks before carriers that print 3-4 weeks after quarter end. ideas.sector_focus: Healthcare services: acute-care, behavioral, rehabilitation and LTCH operators, travel-nurse staffing, hospital supply
ideas.mechanism: Since the November 2024 CMS condition of participation, every hospital reports weekly bed capacity, occupancy and admissions to CDC's NHSN, and CDC publishes jurisdiction-level weekly totals within about a week of the week's end. Hospital operators' quarterly revenue is same-facility admissions times revenue per admission, so weighting each state's occupancy and admissions change by the share of an operator's beds in that state (from the CMS Hospital Enrollments file, which lists each facility's legal entity and state, mapped to the parent via Exhibit 21) gives an operator-specific volume index that is final about ten days after quarter end, three to four weeks before the print. Occupancy also drives contract-labour demand for staffing firms. The facility-level NHSN HRD file that the gap assumed could not be found in the open-data catalogue (UNKNOWN), so this version is state-weighted rather than facility-exact.
ideas.measurement_window: Full fiscal quarter of weekly readings; the quarter's last week is published about 6 days after it ends (TESTED HERE 2026-11-11: latest weekendingdate 2026-10-31 for all jurisdictions; dataset updated 2026-11-06). Operators print 4-5 weeks after quarter end.

ideas.cost: $0 (Socrata app token free).
ideas.who_already_knows: Hospital analysts use the respiratory share of admissions (the S09 content), the operators' own mid-quarter commentary, Strata/Kaufman Hall monthly flash reports (paid, aggregate) and Medicare claims (lagged); state-weighted NHSN occupancy by operator is not in current previews (REASONED, per the brief). Occupancy itself is a public weekly number, so the national level is known; the operator-specific weighting and the quarter-end total are the unpriced part.
ideas.vendors_selling_similar: Kaufman Hall / Strata (National Hospital Flash Report, aggregate), Definitive Healthcare (facility reference data, paid). No vendor is known to sell NHSN-based operator volume indices (UNKNOWN).
ideas.why_ours_differs: Free weekly official reporting rolled up to the listed operator by bed-weighted state footprint, available ten days after quarter end; cheaper and faster than claims-based or survey-based volume estimates, though coarser than the facility file would be.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: A year-on-year change of at least 2 percentage points in bed-weighted NHSN inpatient occupancy (and at least 3% in weighted total admissions) over the fiscal quarter for an operator's state footprint, measured 10 days after quarter end (at least 20 days before the print), predicts a same-sign same-facility admissions and revenue surprise versus final consensus and a same-sign T-1 to T+1 abnormal return versus XLV (opposite sign for contract-labour cost at the operator, same sign for staffing-firm revenue), controlling for the respiratory-admission share, consensus revisions, sector, size and momentum.
ideas.industry_context: Hospital operators' quarters are driven by admissions volume and the mix of payers, and most of them are concentrated in a handful of states; since late 2024 every hospital must report bed occupancy and admissions weekly to CDC, which publishes state totals within a week. A state's occupancy change is therefore a close proxy for the operator's own facilities when the operator holds a large share of that state's beds.
ideas.strongest_reason_wrong: State totals are dominated by non-profit systems whose volumes may not move with the listed operator's, so the bed-weighted index could be a market-wide seasonality proxy already captured by the respiratory share; operators guide on volumes and give mid-quarter colour at conferences; and without the facility-level file the universe is seven operators plus two staffing names, too few for a stand-alone test.
ideas.canonical_name: NHSN weekly state-level inpatient occupancy and admissions, bed-weighted to each operator's state footprint from CMS Hospital Enrollments, as a quarterly volume nowcast for hospital, rehab, LTCH and behavioral operators and healthcare staffing firms

vet.revised_hypothesis: Not restated as a live signal. If revived only as a validation study: bed-weighted (POS CRTFD_BED_CNT) year-on-year change in state pctinptbedsocc over the fiscal quarter, computed from weeks with at least 85% of hospitals reporting in both base and current year (so Q4-2025 onward only), predicts same-sign same-facility adjusted-admissions surprise for THC, UHS, CYH, ARDT, controlling for the NHSN flu/COVID/RSV admission share and consensus revisions. The admissions leg of the original hypothesis is dropped because no all-cause admissions field exists.
vet.reject_reason: The hypothesis as written cannot be measured: NHSN HRD publishes all-cause occupancy (a census) but admissions only for confirmed COVID, flu and RSV, so the 'at least 3% change in weighted total admissions' test has no data behind it, and occupancy = admissions x length of stay diverges from the adjusted-admissions metric operators guide on. The proxy quality is poor: state totals are dominated by non-profit systems and the listed operators are a small minority of beds in nearly every state (REASONED; HCA, the one large for-profit, is outside the universe), so the bed-weighted index mostly measures other people's hospitals, i.e. regional respiratory seasonality that analysts already read directly from the same public NHSN pathogen series. The year-on-year base is broken for the only recent history: May-Oct 2024 had ~36% of hospitals reporting (TESTED HERE), making Q2-Q3 2025 comparisons unusable, and 2026 reporting compliance has slid from 89% to 80% for the newest week, so level counts drift with the panel. Universe is 9 names (not 20-25) and roughly 4 clean quarters, far too few for a stand-alone test; the pre-2024 facility file is COVID-distorted. Lead time is 10-17 calendar days (THC prints ~3 weeks after quarter end), not 21, and the quarter's last week is ~80% complete when first published. Data is free and legal, but I would not stake effort on it ahead of the other candidates.
vet.changes_made: Vendor/literature web searches could not be run: this turn's shared WebSearch budget was exhausted before my calls, so vendors_found and literature_found are empty rather than guessed; the candidate's own Kaufman Hall / Strata and Definitive Healthcare references were not independently seen. Data checks: verified the NHSN field list (no all-cause admissions), hospitals-reporting counts across the 2024 regime change and 2026 erosion, absence of any facility-level NHSN HRD dataset in both Socrata catalogs, the CMS Enrollments header (no beds), the CMS POS file as the correct bed-weight source, and the PBJ ~4-month lag. Lowered signal_noise 2 to 1, lead time 21 to 12 calendar days, universe 20-25 names to 9, confidence 12 to 8. Legal risk stays 1 (US government public-domain data, Socrata token optional).
vet.red_team: The bed-weighted state occupancy index is a proxy for regional respiratory-season intensity, which is already public in the same NHSN release (flu/COVID/RSV admissions) and already used in sell-side hospital previews, while the operator-specific residual is unobservable because the listed operators hold a small share of each state's beds and NHSN has no all-cause admissions at all; any apparent predictive power in a backtest would therefore be the respiratory-share factor plus a broken 2024 base (36% reporting panel) masquerading as an operator volume nowcast, and with ~9 names and ~4 clean quarters nothing would survive a factor control.

gaps.description: Homebuilders are absent. Closings (the quarter's revenue) and starts (next quarter's deliveries) are recorded in county permit, certificate-of-occupancy and deed files under the builders' subsidiary LLC names within days of the event. Zonda and John Burns sell field-survey starts and closings at scale, but the county exhaust is cheaper, daily and lot-level, and sell-side anchors on the builders' own order disclosures (REASONED). Lead time: quarter-end CO counts are final 3-4 weeks before the print.

concerns: Lens skew: regulatory 16, digital 10, physical 8, second_order 5. Second-order is thin and two of its five (N39 lock-up overhang, N58 KEX via TCEQ) are not nowcasts of the quarter; physical ideas are concentrated in one- or two-name energy/materials/agri series (N04, N05, N16, N17).

Effective count is lower than 39. Six kept ideas largely duplicate kept seeds or each other (N58 first-order test = N02; N03 = the NPDES leg of S07; N10 = S16; N27 overlaps S31; N09 overlaps S27; N22/N26 overlap S24), N35 is a conditioning variable and N39 is a flow overlay like S35 (fails criterion (a)). De-duplicated, roughly 31 distinct new signal families remain, still above the 25 floor but the program should not count overlaps twice.

Statistical power: 16 of 39 ideas cover 8 or fewer names (N04 1, N05 1, N16 1, N17 1, N63 2-3, N43 2-3, N49 2, N50 2-3, N51 2-3, N12 3, N07 3-4, N15 5-6, N65 5-6, N36 7, N29 7-8, N53 6-8), i.e. 4-32 events a year each. None can be validated individually for a 2-10 day trade after costs; they should be pooled into a 'single-site physical throughput' family with one test harness and a minimum event count before any is traded.

Inconsistency with seed verdicts: N33 (App Store userRatingCount velocity) is the same mechanism S21 was rejected for (rating-prompt and Apple-reset contamination, snapshot-only, panel proxy); the 'transaction-prompted apps' distinction is thin. Either drop N33 or restrict it to the review-text outage/price-change angle S21's verdict left open.

Inconsistency on blocked sources: N28 and N29 keep chains and OEMs that returned 403 (Planet Fitness, Shake Shack, CAVA, Mister Car Wash, Five Below, Texas Roadhouse, Boot Barn, Polaris) and propose browser or residential fetch, which is the exact workaround that made N31 a legal-4 reject. Per-site ToS and robots.txt must be checked before those names count toward coverage; the honest N28 coverage today is 4 chains, not 40-50.

No Phase-1 backtest path for about 9 ideas (N07/N08 until MOPS history is re-derived, N28 beyond Common Crawl, N29, N33, N35, N48 if Milled fails, N62, N63, N09 Docker Hub/Homebrew legs). S30, S36, N47 and N61 were rejected partly for 'no history', so these should be labelled forward-collection-only and not counted toward the 25.

Common Crawl is load-bearing for N28 backfill, N32 panel discovery and all of N65, yet the N61 probe reported every CDX query reset or timed out from the container. Verify CDX and WARC range access before relying on it; otherwise N65 has no source.

Crowding not stated or understated: N55 (PPI) relies on the series S26's verdict called 'widely published, already modelled by sell-side'; N36 Komtrax and JMTBA orders are quoted in every machinery preview; N18 broiler placements and N17 USDA potato data are the standard sell-side inputs; N15 NRC status is watched in real time by PJM power traders; N12 EIA-860M transitions are tracked by SEIA/Wood Mac. Each needs an explicit 'who already knows / how much is priced' line and a measured gap versus consensus, as the brief requires.

Lead-time plausibility: N09, N48 and N62 claim 1 day, which barely meets criterion (b) and for N62 is meaningless (FedRAMP transitions are not quarter-aligned and no endpoint exists). N17 (4 days) depends on one Cold Storage release landing before LW's early-month print. N27's and N39's lead times describe news events already priced on the filing day; the earnings-window residual is REASONED, not shown.

Legal amber flags inside the kept list: N58 notes TCEQ robots.txt Disallow: / but N02 (same database) is silent on it; N63 depends on ICANN CZDS terms that restrict use and redistribution and on per-registry approval (REASONED, not read); N48 backfill via Milled has UNKNOWN terms; N29 OEM dealer-inventory tools have unchecked ToS; N35 and N07/N39 lean on the Nasdaq calendar despite its robots flag (use EDGAR-derived expected dates as primary).
